topic: Respiratory Organs and the Human Respiratory System
title: Where Does Your Breath Go? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Breathe on a cold mirror and it fogs. A fish gulps water all day, and an earthworm has no nose at all. Diya asks: how does each animal get oxygen, and where does the air go after it enters her nose?

We see why we breathe, zoom from the chest to a lung and the alveoli, and follow the five steps of respiration. Then the path of the air through the human respiratory system, the conducting part vs the exchange part, the pleura and the air-tight thoracic chamber with a pause and think, a worked example on the respiratory organs of animals, the exam trap about cartilage rings, an original NEET pattern match question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 96 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Three animals, three ways to breathe
0:39 Why do we breathe?
0:58 Zoom ladder: chest, lung, alveoli
1:24 The five steps of respiration
2:03 The path of the air
2:28 Conducting part vs exchange part
2:47 Pleura, thoracic chamber + pause and think
3:24 Worked example: which organ?
3:52 Exam trap: complete rings?
4:12 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:36 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Mechanism of Breathing and Respiratory Volumes. What makes air rush into your lungs, and how much air can they really hold?
